name: AD7779ACPZ
title: 8-channel, 24-bit simultaneous sampling Σ-Δ ADC with per-channel PGA and SAR diagnostics
summary: The AD7779 holds eight Σ-Δ converters that sample at the same instant, each with its own PGA (×1, ×2, ×4, ×8) and sinc3 filter, at up to 16 kSPS per channel. A sample rate converter sets the output rate in steps fine enough to follow a drifting line frequency. It has a 2.5 V reference, two power modes, a 12-bit SAR converter for diagnostics, and either strap-pin or SPI configuration, with results on dedicated DOUT lines or over SPI.
key_figures: internal 2.5 V, ±10 ppm/°C typ; external 1 V to AVDD1x
86 mW typ (HR, 16 kSPS), 27 mW typ (LP, 4 kSPS)
AVDD1x 3.0 V to 3.6 V (or ±1.65 V), AVDD2x 2.2 V to 3.6 V, IOVDD 1.8 V to 3.6 V

circuits.title: Pin control mode with an external reference
circuits.description: The AD7779 runs from straps alone. MODE3 to MODE0 pick decimation, power mode, PGA gains and the reference; CONVST_SAR, FORMAT1 and FORMAT0 pick the output format and DCLK2 to DCLK0 the DCLK divider. An outside reference feeds REF1+ and REF2+ with REF1− and REF2− on AVSSx. Conversions leave on DRDY, DCLK and DOUT0 to DOUT3 to an FPGA or DSP acting as a serial slave, which also drives START and RESET and can read conversions over CS, SCLK and SDO; SDI is grounded. SYNC_OUT loops back to SYNC_IN. Every supply pin has its own capacitor; the three LDO outputs take 1 μF. A crystal sits across XTAL1 and XTAL2, or a clock source drives XTAL2.

parts.note: or an external clock source on XTAL2

notes: DCLK2/SCLK, DCLK1/SDI and DCLK0/SDO carry both the DCLK divider straps and the SPI lines; one function per pin is used at a time.
AVDD1x, AVDD4 and AVDD2x share the 3.3 V analog supply.

circuits.title: SPI control mode with the internal reference
circuits.description: FORMAT1 and FORMAT0 tied to IOVDD put the AD7779 under SPI control. REF_OUT drives REF1+ and REF2+ from the internal 2.5 V reference, REF1− and REF2− sit on AVSSx. An FPGA or DSP is the SPI master on CS, SCLK, SDO and SDI, starts SAR conversions on CONVST_SAR, and also receives DRDY, DCLK and DOUT0 to DOUT3. GPIO0 to GPIO2 and the SAR inputs AUXAIN± are brought out for diagnostics. Supplies, LDO capacitors, clock and the SYNC_OUT to SYNC_IN loop match the pin control case.

parts.note: or an external clock source on XTAL2

notes: AVDD1x, AVDD4 and AVDD2x share the 3.3 V analog supply.

operation.text: Eight Σ-Δ modulators sample together, each behind its own capacitive PGA (gain 1, 2, 4 or 8) and followed by a sinc3 filter with a sample rate converter and per-channel gain and offset scaling. Conversion begins on its own once the internal LDO rails are up; no start signal is needed. High resolution mode reaches 16 kSPS; low power mode reaches 8 kSPS with figures guaranteed to 4 kSPS.

Inputs may be true differential, pseudo differential or single ended, bipolar or unipolar. Each AINx pin must stay between AVSSx + 100 mV and AVDD1x − 100 mV; beyond that linearity falls off, and past the absolute maximum the part is damaged. The PGA common mode does not depend on gain. VCM provides (AVDD1x + AVSSx)/2 for single-supply and pseudo or true differential drive.

The PGA is chopped at 64 kHz in high resolution mode and 16 kHz in low power mode to cut offset, drift and 1/f noise; the sinc filter removes the tone. Input bandwidth should be held to 2/3 of the chop frequency to keep intermodulation images out of band.

The internal 2.5 V reference (10 ppm/°C typical) is off at power-up. When on, its buffered output on pin 49 can supply 10 mA continuous and needs 100 nF. For lower noise, a filter below 10 Hz from REF_OUT into REFx+ (REFx− to AVSSx) is used, with the reference buffers in enabled or precharge mode. ADR441 and ADR4525 are named as external references.

Three modes. Enabled: the buffer carries the load, headroom ±100 mV from the rails. Bypassed: the external source charges the ADC reference capacitors directly, and crosstalk worsens because channels are no longer isolated. Precharge (default): the buffer charges the capacitors early in acquisition and the reference finishes the job, lowering reference current against bypass and removing buffer noise against enabled; headroom limits do not apply.

Two analog LDOs and one digital LDO need 1 μF each on AREG1CAP, AREG2CAP and DREGCAP. Their rise follows the main supply, so a RESET pulse after power-up is needed for a correct digital start. Each LDO can be bypassed and its CAP pin driven directly within the LDO bypassing table limits.

All eight ADCs share MCLK, at most 8192 kHz in high resolution and 4096 kHz in low power mode, divided by 4 or 8 to the modulator clock. An internal oscillator loads the registers at power-up, then CLK_SEL chooses a CMOS clock on XTAL2/MCLK (XTAL1 to DGND) or a crystal across XTAL1 and XTAL2. Below 250 kHz external clock, CLK_QUAL_DIS is set (SPI control only). DCLK is MCLK divided by 1 to 128.

A pulse on SYNC_IN resets the digital block without touching register contents. It is needed after writing power mode, offset, gain or phase settings, and to align several parts, in which case it must be synchronous with MCLK. A synchronous pulse can come from START (retimed and sent out on SYNC_OUT) or from GENERAL_USER_CONFIG_2 bit 0; SYNC_OUT is then wired to SYNC_IN. One SYNC_OUT can drive several devices sharing MCLK. Mode pins are re-read at each SYNC_IN pulse. Holding SDI high for 64 clocks resets the part in software.

The sinc3 filter gives low latency and puts notches at the maximum ODR (16 kHz or 8 kHz) and two at the selected ODR. The SRC allows non-integer decimation; the ODR can change on the fly and takes effect after three conversions with no out-of-range results.
Pulling AVDD2 to ground with 1 MΩ from XTAL2 to ground places the part in shutdown, drawing about 1 mA.

MODE3 to MODE0 set power mode, decimation, PGA gain (in blocks of four channels) and reference at power-up. SRC, diagnostics and extended error sources are unavailable. CONVST_SAR, FORMAT1 and FORMAT0 choose SPI or DOUTx output; DCLK2 to DCLK0 set the DCLK divider. The header is always the CRC header.

FORMAT0 and FORMAT1 high select it. Adds per-channel offset, gain and phase correction, SRC, SAR access, GPIOs, diagnostics, drive strength, LDO bypass and CRC. SPI runs in Mode 0 or Mode 3 in multiples of 8 bits: R/W bit, 7-bit address, 8 data bits, plus an 8-bit CRC when SPI_CRC_TEST_EN is set. SDO returns a 0010 0000 header then data. Sending 0x8000 is a harmless read command for streaming SAR or Σ-Δ results without writing registers.

CHx_SYNC_OFFSET delays the start of a channel's filter by a number of modulator clocks to match phase between channels; the leading channel is set to zero and lagging ones delayed. The register is read at the next SYNC_IN pulse and is scaled internally by n from the phase adjustment table.

GENERAL_USER_CONFIG_1 bit 6 selects high resolution or low power; a SYNC_IN pulse must follow a change. VCM, reference buffers, SAR, oscillator and each Σ-Δ channel can be turned off separately. Changing the Σ-Δ reference also calls for a SYNC_IN pulse to drop invalid samples.

Detected faults raise ALERT and the alert bit in the data header; both clear when the fault goes, except SPI faults, which clear on reading GEN_ERR_REG_1. Monitors cover MCLK handover, reset detect, LDO supply monitors, ROM and register map CRC, reference detect (below 0.7 V between REFx+ and REFx−), input overvoltage above AVDD1x + 40 mV and undervoltage below AVSSx − 40 mV, modulator saturation (20 identical codes), filter saturation (about 20% past full scale), output clipping, and SPI CRC, clock count and invalid address faults. ROM or register map CRC faults and modulator saturation need a reset.

A 12-bit, 256 kSPS SAR on its own AVDD4/AVSS4 supply, which is also its reference, checks the chip and the Σ-Δ results. CONVST_SAR starts a conversion (256 kHz maximum) and can be deglitched. Its mux reaches AUXAIN± or internal nodes, some divided by 6. Available in SPI control only; each result is read before the next conversion. The GPIOs can steer an external dual 8:1 mux to route the eight inputs to AUXAIN.

A mux ahead of each PGA can apply zero scale, positive or negative full scale or a 280 mV signal, selected by CHx_RX or CHx_REF_MONITOR and MTR_MUX_CTRL, to check a channel or calibrate gain and offset.

Each channel sends 32 bits: an 8-bit header then 24-bit twos complement data, MSB first. A disabled channel sends 0x000000. DRDY marks each new result whichever interface is used; unread SPI data is overwritten by the next conversion. On DOUTx the AD7779 is the master; with daisy-chaining, DOUT2 (and DOUT3) become inputs fed from the next device's DOUT0 (and DOUT1). The Σ-Δ CRC covers 56 bits per channel pair and is split across the two headers.
DCLK must be fast enough to clear all data before the next result; with a ratio faster than needed, zeros fill the gap.

After writing SRC_N and SRC_IF, the new rate loads either by holding SRC_LOAD_UPDATE high for at least two MCLK periods, or, with SRC_LOAD_SOURCE set, by a pulse on GPIO2 that is retimed and sent out on GPIO1, which is wired to GPIO0; one GPIO1 can drive several devices sharing MCLK.
